---
title: "Treemaps"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8.8, fig.height = 3.3, dpi = 100,
  fig.retina = 2, dev = "ragg_png", out.width = "100%"
)
options(gglaplot2.font = "inter")
library(ggplot2)
library(gglaplot2)
```

A treemap shows part-to-whole data as tiles sized to their value. The web
charts draw them squarified, so the tiles stay close to square, largest
first from the top left, with a one pixel gap between tiles and the label
inside the tile where it fits. They are for a reader to see which parts
are big and which are small at a glance; a bar chart is the better choice
when the values need comparing with any precision.

## One level

Map the value to `area` and the name to `label`. The axes carry nothing,
so `theme_gla_map()` is the theme.

```{r one}
d <- data.frame(
  borough = c("Camden", "Hackney", "Islington", "Barnet", "Brent", "Ealing", "Harrow",
              "Sutton", "Merton", "Bexley"),
  area = c("Inner", "Inner", "Inner", "Outer", "Outer", "Outer", "Outer", "Outer", "Outer",
           "Outer"),
  value = c(42, 35, 28, 51, 44, 39, 22, 9, 15, 11)
)

ggplot(d, aes(area = value, label = borough)) +
  geom_gla_treemap() +
  gla_labs(title = "Ten boroughs by a value", subtitle = "Synthetic data",
           source = "Demo data") +
  theme_gla_map()
```

## Grouped

Map `fill` to the parent category and the tiles are laid out group by
group, each group's tiles together, with the categorical palette telling
the groups apart. The web charts prefer centred labels; `label_position =
"topleft"` puts them in the corner for a denser chart.

```{r grouped}
ggplot(d, aes(area = value, label = borough, fill = area)) +
  geom_gla_treemap(label_position = "topleft") +
  scale_fill_gla() +
  gla_labs(title = "Inner and Outer London", subtitle = "Synthetic data",
           source = "Demo data") +
  theme_gla_map(legend = "top")
```

A tile smaller than `min_label` of the whole (two per cent by default) gets
no label, so the small tiles stay readable as shapes rather than as
overlapping text. The tiles are squarified for the chart's shape; pass
`aspect` if the chart is far from the web charts' 16 by 6.
